subject: Next steps — hosting options & SOC2/BAA gap prioritization
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <dcho@medicahealth.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps — hosting options & SOC2/BAA gap prioritization

Thanks again for your time earlier, Daniel and Elena — helpful call. Below is a concise recap and suggested next steps so we can prioritize the security evidence and choose an operational hosting path that matches Medica's PHI requirements.

Quick recap (options we discussed)
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live, no customer-managed network; available SOC2 evidence in our pack but requires strict application-level de-identification for PHI workflows.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation; good compromise for PHI with an aggressive SLA; Redwood can enable stricter retention controls and dedicated tenancy.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full customer network control and KMS/HSM integration; required for customers that cannot route PHI outside their VPC. More onboarding and procurement.

Security / compliance asks you raised
- BAA requirement for any PHI handling
- SOC2 Type 2 evidence for our continuous controls (audit window and scope)
- Data residency and audit log retention window (we noted US-East preference)

Suggested immediate next steps
1) Please confirm which hosting modes are acceptable in priority order (e.g., Private VPC preferred, Dedicated fallback, Hosted only if de-identified).
2) I attached an evidence matrix (redwood-deploy-evidence-matrix.xlsx) mapping which docs we can provide quickly vs which need a short lead time.
3) Karthik — can you confirm the earliest we can produce SOC2 artifact extracts and the estimated timeline for a BAA draft?
4) Neha — can you own legal touchpoint once they confirm preferred path?

Attachments: redwood-deploy-evidence-matrix.xlsx (matrix), SOC2-type2_2027-Q2.pdf (SOC2 snapshot)

Proposed timeline: once hosting preference is confirmed, we schedule a technical deep dive (60 min) with Karthik next week to walk firewall/network requirements and keys.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Next steps — hosting options & SOC2/BAA gap prioritization

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 
- Priority hosting preference: 1) Private VPC (preferred) 2) Dedicated capacity (acceptable) 3) Hosted API (only for de-identified datasets).
- BAA: required before any PHI is transmitted to Redwood. We need an editable draft to run past Medica legal.
- SOC2: we need evidence of the last 12 months of controls (control objectives + auditor report). The snapshot you attached helps — we’ll review and come back with follow-ups.

Questions for Redwood team:
1) For Private VPC, can Redwood support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and an on-prem option for the inference nodes?
2) For Dedicated capacity, what are retention defaults for logs and how configurable are S3 retention/erasure policies?
3) What is the typical timeline to get a BAA signed from Redwood side (we estimate legal review + signatures ~2–3 weeks if draft is stable)?

We are aiming for a compliance gating decision by 2027-11-15 so we can lock procurement timelines. Please respond with quick feasibility answers and we’ll book the technical deep dive after that.

—Daniel
Daniel Cho

Subject: Re: Next steps — hosting options & SOC2/BAA gap prioritization

Thanks, Daniel — quick technical notes and what we can deliver immediately.

Private VPC / on-prem
- BYOK/KMS: supported for Private VPC and on-prem. We integrate with customer KMS via standard KMIP and can support Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, and common HSM vendors.
- On-prem: Redwood provides an appliance image and orchestration bundle; requires network peering configuration and an initial ops window (2–4 weeks) to provision.

Dedicated capacity
- Retention defaults: audit logs are stored for 90 days by default; retention is configurable up to 7 years via customer request and can be automated with lifecycle policies.
- KV cache and model weights are tenant-isolated; we offer per-tenant encryption at rest.

Hosted API (for completeness)
- Only for de-identified data; we cannot route PHI in our shared-hosted environment without a BAA and additional tenancy controls.

SOC2 artifacts and timeline
- Attached: SOC2-type2_2027-Q2.pdf (full report), and an evidence index. We can provide redacted control evidence extracts within 48–72 hours for initial review (system configurations, access logs, runbooks).
- For auditor-signed artifacts beyond the report (e.g., evidence bundles), plan for a 5–10 business day window for coordination.

BAA and legal
- We have a BAA template; I’m attaching a draft (BAA-draft-Redwood-Medica.docx) to speed review. Neha will be the primary contact for edits/negotiation from our side.

Estimated ramp timelines (from commitment)
- Dedicated capacity: 2–3 weeks to provision reserved pool + network rules; easier procurement path.
- Private VPC / on-prem: 3–6 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS handover.

Attachments provided: SOC2-type2_2027-Q2.pdf, redwood-deploy-evidence-matrix.xlsx, BAA-draft-Redwood-Medica.docx

If that aligns, propose the deep technical session Tuesday 2027-11-09 10:00–11:00 PT to walk Private VPC checklist and handover steps.

—Karthik
